A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FluoCLIP framework and FluoMix dataset. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, tables, and algorithm, are readable and support reliable comparison despite reflow and consolidation.

before.justification: v1 reports original spatial-frequency analyses, benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and supplementary few-shot and cross-tissue/stain experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds CLIP, PubMedCLIP, and PMC-CLIP comparisons on FluoMix.

M1.justification: The two-stage grounding/ranking procedure, stain conditioning, interpolation, losses, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Figure 2 adds a frozen-image-encoder marker for Stage 1, consistent with the updates already specified in v1's algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FocusPath, BBBC006, and the same FluoMix tissues and stains, including the same few-shot and cross-tissue/stain scenarios. Newly stated dataset totals document existing coverage; they do not establish additional data or tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds CLIP to the FluoMix ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 comparisons in Tables 2–3, and PubMedCLIP and PMC-CLIP in supplementary Table 14. Existing comparators, including BiomedCLIP and the few-shot CoOp variants, remain.

E3.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 revise the stated FluoMix protocol from 32-plane stacks with uniformly partitioned labels to 34-plane stacks with relative-position labels. The appendix already specified 34 planes in v1, so this resolves inconsistent reporting without establishing a rerun. New Table 14 specifies each biomedical comparator's own pretrained ResNet50 encoder; retained splits, budgets, and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 compares four stains at focus levels 0, 4, and 9, adding qualitative evidence about appearance differences at matched ranks. Existing component, adapter, backbone, and few-shot transfer analyses remain; v1's supplementary Table 14 ablation is consolidated into v2's Table 6.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five runs/seeds and retain the same spatial-frequency dispersion reporting. Table 6's error bars already appeared in v1's supplementary Table 14. Added baseline rows follow the existing reporting practice; no new statistical procedure or increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: New FluoMix accuracies include CLIP at 81.59±0.52% with ResNet50 and 89.13±0.26% with ViT-B/16, PubMedCLIP at 81.48±0.34%, and PMC-CLIP at 84.06±0.23%. Table 6 corrects plain/trainable stain-token accuracies from 82.47/80.05% to 83.21/81.38%, matching values already present in v1's supplementary Table 14. Retained FluoCLIP benchmark and few-shot results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The ordinal definitions, conditioning/interpolation equations, objectives, and spatial-frequency definition in Equations 1–11 are unchanged. The added diffraction-limit discussion supplies physical motivation, without introducing a new formal result, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the stain-aware FQA formulation, FluoMix as the first corresponding dataset, and a two-stage FluoCLIP framework with strong fluorescence performance and generalization. The critique of a universal ordinal mapping and separation of stain semantics from ranking already appear in v1; v2 emphasizes these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a wavelength-dependent diffraction/PSF explanation and an approximately 1.6-fold theoretical-resolution argument. New Section 14 interprets the biomedical comparisons as evidence that domain pretraining alone is insufficient. The conclusion retains the predefined-stain assumption but omits v1's explicit statement about limitations on entirely unseen stains or imaging modalities.

D1.justification: v2 replaces dataset-size placeholders with approximately 56,000 images and 28 stain–target–tissue channels, adds composition totals, and supplies a project link stating public code/data availability. Conversely, Section 6.1 removes the RAdam optimizer, cosine scheduler, and random prompt-initialization disclosures. Detailed appendix acquisition protocols and sample splits remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to PubMedCLIP, PMC-CLIP, and PubMedBERT and more explicitly distinguishes biomedical pretraining from ordinal focus modeling. Existing cited works and the central stain-aware research positioning remain despite substantial condensation of related-work prose.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introductory passages, both related-work subsections, and conclusion are extensively rewritten or condensed. Affiliations are expanded, acknowledgments are added, and supplementary ablation discussions receive numbered subheadings. This is substantial narrative editing even though the principal section order and scientific method remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 4 and the biomedical comparison table, relocates Figure 1 to the first page, and consolidates v1's supplementary ablation table into Table 6. It also revises Table 6's columns/checkmarks, adds CLIP rows to Tables 2–3, and updates Figure 2's freezing annotation. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful baseline controls and qualitative evidence, reconciles Table 6 with the earlier appendix, resolves the 32/34-plane inconsistency, and replaces dataset placeholders with concrete information and access instructions. These improve completeness and internal consistency. The gains are limited because the method, coverage, and principal results remain stable, while removal of optimizer and scheduler details reduces reproducibility information.
